title: Record maximal-order timeout recovery delta
objective: Measure which retained public maximal-order timeouts recover after certification acceleration and preserve exact verified raw evidence

oracles: independent exact lattice verifier against the certified corpus

runs.command: node -e const fs=require("fs");const j=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("bench/results/number-field-maximal-order-timeout-delta-2026-08-17.json","utf8"));if(j.records.length!==34||new Set(j.records.map(r=>r.case_id)).size!==34)throw Error("cardinality");const s=j.checked_summary;if(s.recovered_exact!==3||s.still_timeout!==31||s.other_terminal_states!==0||s.invalid_lattices!==0)throw Error("partition");if(j.records.some(r=>r.status==="ok"&&r.verification?.verified!==true))throw Error("unverified lattice");if(j.diagnostic_vector_010?.status!=="timeout"||j.diagnostic_vector_010?.timeout_ms!==30000)throw Error("diagnostic");console.log("timeout-delta integrity ok")

handoff.summary: Reran the 34 bounded public maximal-order timeouts from the b60ed9aa corpus artifact at c1b31206. Three cases recovered within the unchanged five-second policy and passed independent exact-lattice verification; 31 remained explicit timeouts, with no wrong lattices or other terminal outcomes. Vector 010 also timed out in a fresh worker under the requested 30-second diagnostic bound. The JSON preserves every raw adapter record and the Markdown gives the checked partition and environment identity.
risks: The 31 retained timeouts are bounded performance outcomes, not correctness failures.
This is a Linux x64 measurement artifact on one AMD EPYC 7B13 host; timing classification may vary on other hardware.
next_steps: Use the exact retained-timeout ID list to prioritize remaining local-order and certification performance work.
Repeat the same fixed-policy delta after the next relevant acceleration without replacing the original raw artifact.
